references.text: Peter quotes directly from Deuteronomy 18:18 and applies the prophecy to Jesus Christ, identifying him as the prophet God promised to raise up from among the people.
Stephen refers to Moses' prophecy about a coming prophet like himself and connects this to Israel's expectation of the Messiah.
The Jews asked John the Baptist if he was 'the Prophet,' showing that they were waiting for the fulfillment of the promise in Deuteronomy 18:18.
Philip identifies Jesus as the one Moses wrote about in the Law, a clear reference to the promised prophet.
The crowd confesses that Jesus is 'the Prophet who is to come into the world,' a messianic expectation based on Moses' prophecy.
Some in the crowd said that Jesus truly was 'the Prophet,' referring to the promised prophet like Moses.
God promised to be with Moses' mouth and teach him what he should speak, a pattern repeated in the promise of the coming Prophet.
The Lord puts his words into the mouth of his servant, a parallel to the promise of putting his words into the prophet's mouth.
God touched Jeremiah's mouth and put his words into it, fulfilling the prophetic pattern from Deuteronomy.
The text confirms that no prophet like Moses had arisen in Israel, pointing forward to the ultimate fulfillment.
